newsitem.title: USA: Johnson Controls workers strike at 2 plants.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Controls workers strike at 2 plants.

text.p: Workers at Johnson Controls Inc seat manufacturing plants in Plymouth, Mich., and Oberline, Ohio, went on strike Tuesday morning after talks between the company and the United Auto Workers union over labor agreements stalled, the company said.
The Plymouth plant makes seats for the Ford Motor Co Expedition sport/utility vehicle. The Oberlin plant makes seats for the Ford Econoline van.
Talks stalled early this morning in negotiations aimed at establishing an initial contract at the plants, which received UAW recognition last summer, Milwaukee-based Johnson Controls said.
The company said in a statement it will make every effort to continue seat production at both plants. It said it plans to hire temporary and/or permanent replacement workers at both locations.
No new talks with the UAW are scheduled at this time, the company said.
The Plymouth plant employs about 300 hourly workers and the Oberlin plant employs about 200 hourly workers, the company said.
Johnson Controls said the UAW's demands are far beyond industry standard wage and benefit packages for unionized automotive suppliers.
UAW spokesman Karl Mantyla said the union is seeking wage parity with other seat suppliers such as Lear Corp, which he said pays $14-$16 an hour.
Mantyla would not say what wages Johnson had offered but said the company "did not get close to that."
The company also would not say what it had offered.

Separately, the UAW said Monday that workers at Johnson Controls's Taylor, Mich., plant had filed a series of unfair labor practice charges with the National Labor Relations Board over what it says are company attacks on employees seeking UAW representation.
The company said the UAW has requested representation without a vote at the plant and the company has rejected that request.
The plant has about 400 hourly workers and makes seats for Chrysler Corp's Jeep Cherokee, Wrangler and Grand Cherokee vehicles, Johnson Controls said.
Johnson Controls shares were up 2-1/2 at 88 in early afternoon trading.
